376:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alley or service drive means a minor, permanent, public service way which is used primarily for vehicular service to the back or the side for properties otherwise abutting a street.
Arterial means an arterial street as defined and/or designated in the zoning ordinance or comprehensive plan of the city.
Block means a piece or parcel of land entirely surrounded by public streets, other than alleys, or other major physical barriers.
Concept plan means a drawing which shows the overall concept of a proposed development, and which may include lots and streets in a subdivision or the general location of buildings and improvements for a multifamily or nonresidential project, and which may be drawn to approximate dimensions in a freehand style.
Cul-de-sac means a minor local street having one end open traffic and being permanently terminated by a vehicular turn around.
Driveway means a vehicular access way in private ownership, other than a private street, which provides access to primarily only one property or no more than two single-family detached residences.
Easement means a recorded authorization for a specified purpose by a property owner for the use of any designated part of the real property by another entity.
Erosion control regulations means the city soil erosion and sediment control ordinance.
Final plat means a finished drawing of a subdivision showing completely and accurately all legal and boundary information and certifications required by these regulations and conforming to the Georgia Plat Act.
Georgia DOT means the State of Georgia Department of Transportation.
Grading means the movement, removal, or addition of soil, earth, sand, silt or rock on-site by use of mechanical equipment.
Grubbing means the removal of stumps, roots, and abandoned underground facilities including, but not limited to, utilities, structures, walls, footings, foundations, wells, septic tanks, storage tanks, and pipe.
Health department means the county health department.
Lot means a portion of a subdivision, or any other parcel of land, intended as a unit for transfer of ownership or for development or both. In determining the area and dimensions of a lot, no part of the public right-of-way may be included.
Lot, corner, means a lot abutting upon two or more streets at their intersection.
Lot, double frontage, means a lot, other than a corner lot, abutting upon two or more streets.
Mean sea level means the average height of the sea for all stages of the tide. For purposes of these regulations, the term "mean sea level" is synonymous with National Geodetic Vertical Datum.
Owner means a person having a majority fee simple interest in real property, or a majority interest through any other form of ownership.
Pedestrian way means a right-of-way within a block dedicated to public use, intended primarily for pedestrians and from which motor-propelled vehicles are excluded.
Planning commission means the city planning commission.
Plat means a drawing prepared by a land surveyor that describes and depicts real property boundaries, including, but not limited to, a map, condominium plat, subdivision plat, as-built survey, easement survey, or retracement survey.
Preliminary plat means a drawing which shows the perimeter boundary, topography, lot layout arrangement, street layout, and other features of a proposed subdivision, as specified in these regulations.
Road. Refer to Street, public.
Sketch plan. Refer to Concept plan.
Street, local nonresidential, means a street intended primarily to provide local access to adjacent existing or planned commercial or industrial development and not for through traffic.
Street, local residential, means a street intended primarily to provide local access to adjacent existing or planned residential development and not for through traffic.
Street, major collector, means a through street intended primarily to provide service through nonresidential areas.
Street, marginal access, means a public right-of-way, whether designated as an avenue, boulevard, road, highway, expressway, lane or other way, that is dedicated or devoted to the public pedestrian or vehicular use by deed, plat, and/or prescription, which affords the principal means of access to abutting property.
Street, minor collector, means a through street intended primarily to connect subdivisions or other areas to major collector streets or other thoroughfares, or functioning as a central route within a subdivision channeling traffic from the local streets to a major collector, another minor collector, or other thoroughfares.
Street, private, means an access way, other than a driveway, similar to and having the same function as a public street, providing access to more than one property, but held in private ownership.
Street, public, means a right-of-way dedicated to and accepted by the city for vehicular traffic or over which the city may hold a prescriptive easement for public access, and including designated and numbered U.S. and state highways. Subdivider means any person dividing or proposing to divide land so as to constitute a subdivision as herein defined.
Subdivision means:
(1) As a verb, the term "subdivision" means any division or redivision of a lot, tract or parcel, regardless of its existing or future use, into two or more lots, tracts, or parcels. The term "subdivision" means the act or process of dividing property.
(2) As a noun, the term "subdivision" also may be used in reference to the aggregate of all lots held in common ownership at the time of division.
Zoning regulations means the city zoning ordinance.

(a) For the purpose of these regulations, the types of activities contained in this section shall be considered subdivisions but are exempt from the procedures and required public improvements portions of these regulations, except as noted:

c. Each proposed lot complies with requirements of the health department.
d. No lot thus created may be resubdivided to less than five acres as an exemption to these regulations.
(b) For the purpose of these regulations, the types of activities contained in this section shall be considered subdivisions but are exempt from the procedures and required public improvements portions of these regulations, provided the property owner notifies the city in writing of such division and provides a copy of a plat of the land subdivision prepared and sealed by a land surveyor currently registered in the state. Such notification is to be submitted to the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 3.4, 7-9-2002)
385:
Land subject to flooding, improper drainage or erosion, and any land deemed unsuitable for development due to steep slopes, unsuitable soils, subsurface conditions or other undesirable properties shall not be subjected to development for any uses as may continue such conditions or increase danger to health, safety, life, or property, unless steps are taken to eliminate or abate these conditions. Land within a proposed subdivision that is unsuitable for development shall be incorporated into the buildable lots as excess lot area, unless such land is subject to an easement or other dedication for common open space.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 4.1, 7-9-2002)
386:
Whenever there is a discrepancy between minimum standards or dimensions required under this article and those contained in zoning regulations, development regulations, building codes or other ordinances or regulations, the most restrictive shall apply.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 4.2, 7-9-2002)
387:
(a) All proposed subdivisions shall conform to the adopted comprehensive plan of the city at the time of submission of the preliminary plat to the city.
(b) Where features of the comprehensive plan, such as parks, streets, and utility systems, are located in whole or in part in a proposed subdivision, or when these features have not been anticipated by the comprehensive plan, but are considered essential by the planning commission and/or mayor and council, land for such features shall be dedicated.
(c) The mayor and council shall disapprove subdivisions when such planned features, as specified by the comprehensive plan, are not incorporated therein.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 4.3, 7-9-2002)
388:
(a) All property corners shall be monumented with a steel-concrete reinforcing bar or steel pipe at least one-half inch in diameter and 18 inches long. Standard brass disk survey monuments or concrete state department of transportation right-of-way markers are also acceptable property corner monuments. In areas to be maintained with grass mowing equipment, bar or pipe monuments are to be installed at or within two inches of ground level. In paved areas, bar or pipe monuments are to be installed flush with the pavement surface. In natural areas, bar or pipe monuments are to be installed so as to extend one to four inches above ground level.
(b) On subdivisions containing floodplains, not less than one permanent vertical control monument per ten acres of floodplain area shall be established and identified on the final plat. Each permanent vertical control monument shall be referenced to mean sea level and be standard brass disk type survey monument or concrete state department of transportation right-of-way marker. When right-of-way markers are used, they shall be buried vertically such that three to six inches of the marker extends above ground level.
(c) All property corner and vertical control monuments shall be installed before the final plat is considered for approval by the city.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 4.4, 7-9-2002)
389:
(a) When land is subdivided into larger parcels than ordinary building lots, such lots shall be arranged and designed so as to allow for the opening of future streets and to provide access to those areas not presently served by streets.
(b) Every development shall be designed to facilitate access to adjoining properties which are developed or anticipated to be developed in a manner substantially similar to the subject property. In determining whether a subdivision shall be designated in such a manner which completely eliminates street access of adjoining parcels of land, the following factors shall be considered:
(1) Whether there are adjoining undeveloped properties in which there exists a reasonable opportunity for such properties to be developed in a substantially similar manner.
(2) There are certain ecological or environmental features to the property.
(3) Existing or proposed circulation patterns or public gathering places so justify access.
(4) Existing uses of property.
a. When required locations of interparcel access shall be as required by and subject to the approval of the city, based upon consideration of the factors listed above.
b. If interparcel access is available, it shall not be used to provide access to residential development through industrial development.
c. Any lot required to provide minimum frontage by the zoning district in which the lot is located shall provide vehicular access directly from a public street along the frontage or along any other property line which abuts a public street.
d. Private streets may be approved under the provisions of the zoning ordinance or development regulations and shall be constructed to the roadway standards of the city.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 4.5, 7-9-2002)

4. Islands. In general, use of raised traffic islands is discouraged in favor of painted islands supplemented with traffic buttons or other devices manufactured for traffic control. Where requested by the city engineer, traffic islands shall conform to the design guidance of the latest edition of "A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets," published by the American Association of Highway and Transportation Officials. (i) Provide not less than 150 feet of storage length for arterial roadways. Provide not less than 100 feet of storage length for collector roadways.
(ii) Provide taper lengths of not less than 50 feet.
(iii) Longer storage and taper lengths may be required when traffic projections indicate they are justified.

The lengths of cul-de-sac streets may be increased if a variance for such is approved by the mayor and council, utilizing the procedures for variances outlined in the city's zoning regulations.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 5.2, 7-9-2002)
396:
Lots should be designed generally such that they are no more than four times as deep as they are wide at the building setback line. For lots which include unusual building sites due to easement configuration, possible floodplain encroachment, stormwater detention facilities, zoning imposed buffers, and/or unusual or severe topographic features, the city may require a final plat notation requiring an approved site plan prior to issuance of a building permit. All lots shall conform to the requirements of the city's zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 6.1, 7-9-2002)
397:
Side lot lines should generally be at right angles or radial to street rights-of-way. In cul-de-sacs, side lot lines should be radial to the center point of the cul-de-sac. When a more efficient use of the land relative to topographic conditions or improved building sites can be achieved by a reasonable lot pattern which does not fully adhere to the desirable side lot line configuration defined in this section, the mayor and council will allow the alternate lot pattern unless specific objections are noted.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 6.2, 7-9-2002)
398:
Corner lots shall have extra width to permit prescribed setback limits from all streets on which the lot has frontage.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 6.3, 7-9-2002)
399:
(a) Double frontage lots other than corner lots shall be required for residential subdivisions along arterial or primary collector streets where internal access can be provided. When approved by the mayor and council, double frontage lots can be used to overcome specific disadvantages of topography, orientation and/or property size. Otherwise, double frontage lots other than corner lots shall be prohibited.
(b) To properly separate residential subdivisions employing double frontage lots from traffic arteries, the mayor and council shall require a planted buffer of 25-foot minimum width along the lot line abutting the traffic artery. The easement for the buffer will be required to deny right of access to the lot on which it is located.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 6.4, 7-9-2002)
400:
(a) The lengths, widths, and shapes of blocks shall be determined with regard to:
(1) Provision of adequate building sites suitable to the special needs of the type of use contemplated.
(2) Applicable zoning requirements as to lot size and dimensions.
(3) Needs for convenient access, circulation, control and safety of vehicular and pedestrian traffic.
(4) Limitations and opportunities topography.
(b) The planning commission may, when existing or proposed pedestrian/bicycle circulation patterns or public gathering places so justify, require pedestrian/bicycle ways or access easements through blocks.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 6.5, 7-9-2002)
403:
(a) The preliminary plat for a subdivision shall be clearly and legibly drawn at a scale of not less than 100 feet to one inch. The sheet size shall not exceed 48 inches by 36 inches; provided, however, a scale of 200 feet to one inch may be used to avoid sheets in excess of 48 inches by 36 inches. The minimum sheet size shall be 8½ inches by 11 inches. The city engineer may approve other scales and sheet sizes as deemed appropriate.
(b) The preliminary plat shall contain the following:
(1) Proposed name of the subdivision.
(2) Names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the property owner of record and the developer or subdivider.
(3) Name, address, and telephone number each professional firm associated with a preliminary plat.
(4) Date of survey, north point and graphic scale.
(5) Subdivision location, including land lot and land district, area in acres, internal and abutting zoning, proposed number of lots with minimum lot size, and proposed phasing, if any.
(6) A location sketch or vicinity map positioning the subdivision in relation to the surrounding area with regard to recognized permanent landmarks. The location sketch scale shall be not greater than 2,000 feet to the inch.
(7) Boundary lines of the overall property perimeter showing bearings in degrees, minutes and seconds and distances in feet and hundredths of a foot along all lines and the bearing and distances to an existing street intersection or other recognized permanent landmark. The source of boundary information shall be shown.
(8) Topography with mean sea level contours at intervals no greater than five feet. The source of topographic information shall be shown.
(9) Natural features, such as lakes, ponds, streams, creeks, state waters, wetlands, 100-year floodplains and other significant features. The source of floodplain information shall be shown.
(10) Cultural features, such as rights-of-way, easements, pavements (including widths), bridges, culverts and storm drains, utility lines, appurtenances and structures, city and county jurisdictional limits, land lot and district lines, zoning districts and limits and other significant features.
(11) Proposed layout, including lot lines with the preliminary dimensions, lot numbers, block letters, street rights-of-way with names and widths, easements, public use facilities, facilities exclusively for subdivision use and all relevant conditions of zoning.
(12) Locations of all known existing or previous landfills.
(13) Proposed method of sewage disposal.
(14) Concept plan certifications as specified in section 26-184.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 7.1, 7-9-2002)
404:
In addition to the preliminary plat, the following information shall be provided to the mayor and council with each preliminary plat submittal:
(1) A written summary of the proposed subdivision giving information as to the overall development plan, including, as appropriate, the types and square footage of structures, number of housing units, types of land uses, anticipated traffic generation, and other pertinent information, so that the effects of the subdivision can be considered by the mayor and council.
(2) Description of the anticipated utility systems required to serve the proposed subdivision, including projected average and peak demands or flows for potable water, fire protection, sewerage and electrical power.
(3) Description of proposed stormwater management practices for the subdivision, including the ownership and proper maintenance provisions of all stormwater detention facilities within the subdivision.
(4) Such additional information as may be reasonably required to obtain an adequate understanding of the subdivision.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 7.2, 7-9-2002)
405:
(a) Subdivision development plans shall generally conform to the approved preliminary plat and may constitute only that portion of the preliminary plan which the developer or subdivider proposes to construct at one time as a single unit or phase, provided that such portion conforms to these regulations.
(b) Subdivision development plans are to consist of not less than the following:
(1) Erosion/sediment control plan prepared in accordance with the city's soil erosion and sediment control ordinance.
(2) Grading and drainage plans prepared in accordance with the city's development regulations.
(3) Street improvement plans prepared in accordance with the city's development regulations.
(4) Utility plans prepared in accordance with the city's development regulations.
(5) Tree protection plan prepared in accordance with the city's tree protection ordinance.
(c) Encroachments. Where construction is proposed on adjacent property, an encroachment agreement or easement shall be submitted to the city.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 7.3, 7-9-2002)
406:
(a) The final plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn in black ink on suitable permanent reproducible material. The scale of the final plat shall be 100 feet to one inch or larger. Sheet size shall not exceed 24 inches by 34 inches. The minimum sheet size shall be 8½ inches by 11 inches.
(b) The final plat shall be based on a certified boundary survey delimiting the entirety of the property contained within the final plat, and tied to a point of reference with the same degree of accuracy as the boundary itself. The survey shall have an accuracy of no less than one in 10,000, and shall meet all requirements of state law regarding the recording of maps and plats.
(c) The final plat shall substantially conform to the approved concept plat and it may constitute only a portion of the approved concept plat which the subdivider proposes to record at any one time, provided that such portion conforms to the requirements of these regulations, and said portion is not inconsistent with public health, safety, or welfare. Any substantial deviation from the approved concept plat shall require revision and reapproval of the concept plat.
(d) The final plat shall contain the following:
(1) Name of the subdivision and unit or phase number, if any.
(2) Names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the property owner of record and the developer or subdivider.
(3) Name, address, and telephone number of each professional firm associated with the portion of the subdivision depicted on the final plat.
(4) Date of plat and survey, north point and graphic scale.
(5) Subdivision location including land lot and land district, area in acres, internal and abutting zoning, and proposed number of lots.
(6) A location sketch or vicinity map positioning the subdivision in relation to the surrounding area with regard to recognized permanent landmarks. The location sketch shall be not greater than 2,000 feet to the inch.
(7) Boundary lines of the subdivision property perimeter showing bearings in degrees, minutes and seconds and distances in feet and hundredths of a foot along all lines and the bearing and distance to an existing street intersection or other recognized permanent landmark. The boundary information shall be tied and related to the State Plane Coordinates System, 1983 North American Datum, Georgia, west zone.
(8) Municipal or county jurisdictional lines tied to the lines of the subdivision; land lot or land district lines traversing or adjoining the subdivision shall also be indicated.
(9) Locations, widths and names of all streets within and immediately adjoining the plat and all other public or utilities easements or rights-of-way.
(10) Street centerlines showing angles of deflection and standard curve data, including radii, chord lengths and bearings, lengths of arcs and tangents, and points of curvature and tangency.
(11) Lot lines with complete dimensions to the nearest one-hundredth of a foot and bearings to the nearest second, and radii, arc and chord lengths, and chord bearings of rounded corners.
(12) Building setback lines with dimensions. When lots are located on a curve or when side lot lines are at angles other than 90 degrees, the lot width at the building line shall be shown.
(13) Lots numbered in numerical order and blocks lettered alphabetically.
(14) Location, material and size of all drainage pipes, location and type of all drainage system appurtenances, such as catchbasins, headwalls, and inlets; location and extent of detention ponds with 100-year event level noted; the location, material and size of all city water mains; the location of all fire hydrants; and location, width and purpose of any easements, including slope easements.
(15) Location of any areas to be reserved, donated, or dedicated to public use with notes stating their purpose and limitations. Location of any areas to be reserved by private deed covenant for common use of all property owners, or dedicated to a homeowners' association.
(16) A statement of private covenants, if any, and if they are brief enough to be put directly on the final plat; otherwise, if covenants are separately recorded, a statement as follows:
This plat is subject to the covenants set forth in the separate document attached hereto dated ________, which hereby become a part of this plat, and which were recorded on ________.
(17) Accurate location, material and description of property corner or line monuments or markers. All monuments and markers shall be in place prior to approval of the final plat.
(18) Extent of the 100-year floodplain within the subdivision. When the floodplain is present, a chart giving the areas within and outside of the floodplain for each lot containing any portion of the floodplain shall be on the final plat. The origin of the floodplain data shall be indicated.
(19) Individual lots which are deemed by the city engineer as requiring site plans shall be designated in a readily identifiable manner.
(20) Certificates and statements specified in these regulations.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 7.4, 7-9-2002)

408:

411:
(a) The schedule of fees for development plan review, copies of these regulations, appeals, waivers, reinspections, and other items are on file with the city clerk and may be altered or amended from time to time by the city council to help defray the costs of the administration of these regulations.

(Ord. No. 2002-02, art. VII, 7-9-2002)
414:
(a) These subdivision regulations shall be administered, interpreted, and enforced by the city clerk or the clerk's designated representative.
(b) In any case in which activities are undertaken in violation of these regulations, not in compliance with the provisions of a permit issued by the city, or without authorization of a permit which would otherwise be required, the city clerk is hereby authorized to order that all unauthorized or improper work be stopped, direct correction of deficiencies, or take any other legal or administrative action appropriate to the severity of the violation and degree of threat to the public health, safety, and welfare.
(c) It shall be the duty and responsibility of the city clerk to maintain an accurate and up-to-date compilation of these subdivision regulations, including appendices, and all amendments, and to publish said compilation and make it available to the public for a fee set by the city council.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 8.1, 7-9-2002)
415:
(a) It is the intention of this section that all questions arising in connection with the interpretation and enforcement of these regulations first be presented to the city clerk and that such questions shall be presented to the city council only on appeal from the decision of the city clerk.
(b) Requests of waivers of the requirements of these regulations shall be submitted in a form as prescribed by the city clerk along with such fee as shall be established by the city council.
(c) The city clerk shall coordinate the review of each waiver request by all other affected city departments and shall summarize such comments and/or recommendations as may be received to the city council for final action in its normal course of business.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 8.2, 7-9-2002)
416:
(a) Any person, firm or corporation violating any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, shall be fined as determined by the judge of the city's criminal court for each offense. Each day such violations continue shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) Nothing herein contained shall prevent the city from taking such other lawful action as is necessary to prevent or remedy any violation.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 8.3, 7-9-2002)
419:
(a) Appeals to the city council may be taken by any person aggrieved or by any officer, department, city council or bureau of the city. Such appeal shall be filed within ten days of the decision complained of by filing with the officer from whom the appeal is taken and with the mayor and council notice of said appeal specifying the grounds thereof. The city clerk shall forthwith transmit to the city council all papers constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken.
(b) An appeal stays all legal proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from, unless the officer from whom the appeal is taken certifies to the city council, after the notice of appeal shall have been filed with the officer, that, by reason of facts stated in the certificate, a stay would, in the officer's opinion, cause imminent peril to life and property. In such case, proceedings shall not be stayed otherwise than by a restraining order, which may be granted by the city council or by a court of record on application, on notices to the officer from whom the appeal is taken, and on due cause shown.
(c) The city council shall fix a reasonable time for the hearing of the appeal or other matter referred to it, and give public notice thereof, as well as due notice to the parties in interest, and decide the same within a reasonable time. At the hearing, any party may appear in person or by agent by attorney.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 9.1, 7-9-2002)
420:
The mayor and council shall have those duties as set forth under the zoning ordinance, as well as any duties assigned to such city council under the provisions of these regulations. Any variances or appeals to the mayor and council shall follow the procedures for such action as set forth under the zoning ordinance applying the standards set forth therein.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 9.2, 7-9-2002)
421:
Any person aggrieved by any decision of the city council approving or denying a preliminary plat or final plat shall have the right of certiorari to the superior court within 30 days after the decision of the city council is rendered.
(Ord. No. 2002-02, § 9.3, 7-9-2002)
424:

Each member of the planning commission will be provided with a copy of each amendment. The planning commission shall have 30 days within which to submit its report after its first consideration. If the planning commission fails to submit a report within the 30-day period, it shall be deemed to have recommended approval of the proposed amendment.

(a) Any condition which causes the normal supply of water pressure to be reduced excessively requires that priority use of water be implemented. These conditions include any of the following:
(1) High water demand.
(2) Drought and excessive heat conditions.
(3) Power failures.
(4) Supply interruptions.
(5) Water main breakage or failures.
(b) A general ranking of water uses in decreasing order of importance would be as follows:
(1) Household use.
(2) Public necessity.
(3) Livestock.
(4) Industrial and commercial.
(5) Construction.
(6) Irrigation.
(7) Non-essential firefighting.
(8) Swimming pools.
(9) Car washing.
(10) Street cleaning, line flushing, hydrant testing, lawn watering, etc.
(c) The city proposes to establish an emergency conservation plan, as outlined in this subsection, which places restrictions on lower priority water usage during periods when water use reduction is urgent. The following subsections outline a drought/emergency conservation plan for the city. The plan is divided into four stages of emergency conditions briefly described as minor, moderate, severe, and critical.
(1) Stage one: Minor emergency condition. The city will, when minor conditions occur, first put the following priority conservation methods in place.
a. Public notices will be placed in places of business throughout the city and in the local newspaper requesting that customers curtail the use of any unnecessary water. This will be primarily aimed at limiting the practice of watering laws, gardens, washing cars and other practices that are not essential during emergency conditions.
b. In addition, fire departments and others will be asked to curtail water main flushing, dust control and other non-essential uses of water. This request is made by the mayor. Under minor conditions, these reductions shall be on a voluntary compliance basis.
(2) Stage two: Moderate water emergency. If conditions degenerate from what was considered a minor condition to a moderate emergency, the following additional steps may be taken:
a. First, the posting of notices would be increased and the newspaper notice would include a release from the mayor explaining the degree of severity of the problem. The mayor will make a stronger appeal for voluntary reductions in water usage.
b. The same water reduction methods that were outlined in the minor emergency section would be implemented in the moderate, with the addition that city crews and, in some cases, public safety officials will be asked to actually field monitor water usage. If customers are observed using water for non-essential purposes, they will be contacted on-site and asked to curtail water use. After two requests are made, if the customer fails to comply, his water service may be disconnected at the meter and a reconnection fee may be charged to return the customer to service.
(3) Stage three: Severe water emergency.
a. In cases where the city deems conservation measures required to be severe, the mayor, as well as the city council, will make appeals to the customers of the system. In addition, news briefings will be given to large users outlining the problem.
b. A much more severe ban on water usage will be required, and prohibition of all public water usage not required for health and safety will be activated. The prohibition will allow no outside water usage that is not absolutely essential for health and safety. No water-cooled air conditions will be allowed to run without recirculation.
c. Businesses, such as car washes and laundromats, will be asked to curtail operations for limited periods. High water using industries will be asked to curtail operations if they operate in more than one shift.
d. The penalties for ignoring the water use warnings will result in shut-off of water service to the customer after one request.
(4) Stage four: Critical.
a. When the emergency becomes critical, measures implemented for a severe emergency will be continued along with additional measures.
b. Prohibitions will be imposed on the use of any water for outside activities not essential or required for health and safety.
c. Any business that is a high water user will be required to curtail operations for limited periods until the water emergency has subsided.
d. The mayor will also issue a request that individual residents conserve in other specific ways.
e. In addition to the personnel of the city, the police department will be asked to monitor unnecessary use of water.
f. The city will take measures to reduce the pressure to the minimum permissible level in areas where it is possible to do so.
g. As a last resort, the city will temporarily terminate service to selected portions of the system at alternate intervals.
(Ord. No. 2018-04, § 1(8), 9-11-2018)
